content_voiceover: This slide from MD Anderson tracks survival in Philadelphia chromosome positive ALL across five treatment eras spanning nineteen eighty four to twenty twenty three, and it's a beautiful illustration of how targeted therapy transformed a once dismal disease. In the pre tyrosine kinase inhibitor era, five year overall survival was only about nine percent with a median survival of just fourteen months. Adding imatinib to hyper C-VAD chemotherapy pushed five year survival to forty two percent, and switching to dasatinib nudged that further to forty eight percent. But the real leap came with ponatinib plus hyper C-VAD, reaching seventy six percent five year survival, and the most recent era combining blinatumomab with ponatinib is tracking even higher, with three year survival around eighty nine percent, essentially chemotherapy free induction. The panel on the right shows a randomized comparison confirming ponatinib beats dasatinib head to head, with event free survival of sixty nine versus forty six percent and overall survival of eighty three versus fifty six percent. The board takeaway is that in Ph positive ALL, potent third generation TKIs like ponatinib, especially paired with immunotherapy, have essentially closed the survival gap that used to separate this subtype from Philadelphia negative disease.
keypoints: Ponatinib + HyperCVAD -> 76% 5yr OS, beats dasatinib head to head
keypoint_voiceover: Remember the survival ladder in Ph positive ALL: roughly nine percent in the pre TKI era, climbing through imatinib and dasatinib into the forties, then jumping to seventy six percent with ponatinib, and now approaching ninety percent when ponatinib is paired with blinatumomab. Ponatinib beat dasatinib directly in a randomized trial for both event free and overall survival.
